# @anyknown/axis

> Headless scroll primitive for horizontal rows, vertical lists and 2D canvases: native scroll first, mouse drag as an enhancement. You give it an element with `overflow: auto`; touch, trackpad, keyboard and scrollbar stay native. axis adds mouse drag-scrolling (x, y or both) with momentum, scroll-snap-aware release, optional wheel-to-horizontal for rows, nested-container hand-off, and an observable scroll state for prev/next buttons and progress bars. Framework-agnostic core plus an optional React hook.

Key facts for writing code with this library:

- Entry points: `@anyknown/axis` (core, `createAxis`) and `@anyknown/axis/react` (`useAxis`). ESM only. React 18 or 19 is an optional peer dependency; the core never imports it.
- No CSS shipped, no required DOM structure, no wrapper elements. The container must be a real scroll container (`overflow-x: auto`, `overflow-y: auto` or `overflow: auto`) that you style yourself.
- The native `scrollLeft` / `scrollTop` is the only source of truth. Nothing is moved with `transform`. There is no looping, no slide effects, no virtualisation.
- Only primary-button mouse drags are taken over (after a 5px threshold). Touch and pen always scroll natively.
- Use CSS `scroll-snap-type` / `scroll-snap-align` for snapping; there is no snap option. axis reads them and settles on snap positions itself.
- All positions are logical: measured from the inline start edge, so they are positive in RTL too.

## Vanilla usage

```ts
import { createAxis } from "@anyknown/axis"

const row = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(".row")! // display:flex; overflow-x:auto
const axis = createAxis(row, { wheel: true })

prev.addEventListener("click", () => axis.scrollPrev())
next.addEventListener("click", () => axis.scrollNext())
const unsubscribe = axis.subscribe((state) => {
	prev.disabled = !state.x.canScrollPrev
	next.disabled = !state.x.canScrollNext
})

// teardown: removes listeners/observers and restores every inline style and attribute axis changed
unsubscribe()
axis.destroy()
```

Vertical list: `createAxis(list, { axis: "y" })`. Pannable canvas: `createAxis(viewport, { axis: "both" })` with one large child.

## React usage

```tsx
import { useAxis } from "@anyknown/axis/react"

function Row({ items }: { items: string[] }) {
	const { ref, state, api } = useAxis<HTMLDivElement>({ wheel: true })
	return (
		<>
			<div ref={ref} className="row">
				{items.map((item) => <div key={item} className="card">{item}</div>)}
			</div>
			<button disabled={!state.x.canScrollPrev} onClick={() => api.scrollPrev()}>Prev</button>
			<button disabled={!state.x.canScrollNext} onClick={() => api.scrollNext()}>Next</button>
		</>
	)
}
```

- `ref` is a stable callback ref. Merge with your own ref inline: `ref={(el) => { mine.current = el; ref(el) }}`.
- The instance is created on mount, destroyed on unmount, and moved when the ref is attached to another element. Options may be an inline object literal; changes are applied in place without re-creating the instance.
- `state` uses `useSyncExternalStore` and is SSR-safe. `api` (`scrollPrev`, `scrollNext`, `scrollTo`, `refresh`) is stable and a no-op before mount.
- Selector to avoid re-rendering on every scrolled pixel: `const { ref, state: canNext, api } = useAxis(undefined, (s) => s.x.canScrollNext)`. Compared with `Object.is`; return a primitive or an existing object (`(s) => s.x`), never a freshly built object/array. Inline selectors are fine (no `useCallback` needed).
- Do NOT pass type arguments together with a selector: `useAxis<HTMLDivElement>(undefined, selector)` does not compile. Omit them; `ref` then accepts any HTML element.

## API

`createAxis(el: HTMLElement, options?: AxisOptions): AxisInstance`

```ts
type AxisMode = "x" | "y" | "both"
type AxisName = "x" | "y"

interface AxisOptions {
	axis?: AxisMode // default "x". "x" ignores vertical mouse movement, "y" the mirror, "both" pans freely in 2D
	momentum?: boolean // default true. Glide after a fast drag. Never applied under prefers-reduced-motion
	wheel?: boolean // default false. Vertical wheel -> horizontal scroll. ONLY used with axis: "x"; ignored otherwise
	cursor?: boolean // default true. cursor: grab / grabbing on the container
}

interface AxisInstance {
	getState(): AxisScrollState // replaced (never mutated) when a value changes
	subscribe(listener: (state: AxisScrollState) => void): () => void
	scrollPrev(axis?: AxisName): void // previous snap position, or back 90% of the visible size when not snapping
	scrollNext(axis?: AxisName): void // next snap position, or forward 90% of the visible size
	scrollTo(position: { x?: number; y?: number }, options?: { animate?: boolean }): void // logical px; animate defaults to true
	setOptions(options: AxisOptions): void // partial; missing/undefined keys keep their value
	refresh(): void // re-read layout and snap positions; rarely needed
	destroy(): void
}

interface AxisScrollState {
	x: AxisState // both axes are always reported, whatever `axis` is
	y: AxisState
	isDragging: boolean // a mouse drag is scrolling the container
	isMomentum: boolean // gliding after a drag (momentum or settling on a snap position)
}

interface AxisState {
	scroll: number // logical px from the start edge, 0..maxScroll
	maxScroll: number // 0 when the content fits
	progress: number // scroll / maxScroll, 0..1 (0 when content fits)
	canScrollPrev: boolean // more than 1px from the start edge
	canScrollNext: boolean // more than 1px from the end edge
}
```

Exported types: `AxisInstance`, `AxisMode`, `AxisName`, `AxisOptions`, `AxisPosition`, `AxisScrollState`, `AxisScrollToOptions`, `AxisState` (from both entry points), plus `AxisApi` and `UseAxisResult` from `@anyknown/axis/react`.

## Behaviour and gotchas

- With `axis: "both"`, `scrollPrev()` / `scrollNext()` have no default axis and THROW unless you pass `"x"` or `"y"`.
- `scrollTo` missing axes stay put. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, `scrollTo` and prev/next jump instead of animating.
- Presses inside `input`, `textarea`, `select`, `[contenteditable]` or any element with the `data-axis-no-drag` attribute never start a drag. Use `data-axis-no-drag` on sliders, resize handles, draggable items, etc.
- While dragging, the container has the `data-axis-dragging` attribute (style it with `[data-axis-dragging]`), plus `cursor: grabbing` and `user-select: none`.
- After a real drag, the next `click` is swallowed once (capture phase), so releasing over a link or button does not activate it. Normal clicks (under 5px movement) are unaffected.
- With `wheel: true` on an `"x"` row, at the edge in the wheel's direction the event is left alone so the page scrolls on.
- State updates automatically on scroll, resize (ResizeObserver on container and children) and DOM mutations (children added/removed, `class`/`style`/`dir` changes inside the container, `dir` on ancestors). Call `refresh()` only for changes axis cannot see: a `class` change on an ancestor, or a stylesheet/media query that changes `scroll-padding`, `scroll-margin` or `scroll-snap-align` without resizing anything.
- Only direct children of the container are read as snap areas.
- `proximity` snapping is settled like `mandatory` on drag release.
- Overlay scrollbars (macOS default) cannot be distinguished from content, so a mouse press on an overlay scrollbar thumb starts a drag.
- Horizontal writing modes only. RTL uses the modern `scrollLeft` model (0 to negative); axis converts it to logical positions for x.

## Nested containers

All instances in a window share one coordinator; just call `createAxis` / `useAxis` on each container, no extra setup. When a drag passes the 5px threshold, the coordinator takes its dominant direction and walks instances under the pointer from innermost outwards, giving the drag to the first instance whose `axis` covers that direction and can still scroll that way (edge hand-off like native overscroll chaining). The owner does not change for the rest of the drag.

Kanban pattern: board is `axis: "x"`, each column is `axis: "y"`. Vertical drags scroll the column under the pointer, horizontal drags scroll the board.

## When not to use it

Choose a transform-based carousel (Embla, Keen Slider) instead when you need looping, slide transitions, or full control of motion on touch devices. axis is for native-feeling rows, lists and canvases that also drag with a mouse.
